title: Cybersecurity awareness training requirements by country: Australia, the EU and Portugal, the US and the UAE compared
description: How cybersecurity awareness training duties compare across Australia, the EU and Portugal, the US and the UAE, including board training and annual cycles.
shortAnswer: Cybersecurity awareness training duties in Australia, the EU and Portugal, the United States and the UAE apply by sector, not to every employer. Financial entities, critical and essential service operators, government bodies and defense contractors face explicit duties, often with an annual minimum: New York's Part 500, US federal agencies and Australia's protective security framework all set one. The EU stands out for requiring management body members themselves to be trained, under NIS2 and DORA.
keyTakeaways: Cyber training duties attach to sectors: prudential and financial regulation (APRA CPS 234, DORA, NYDFS Part 500, the FTC Safeguards Rule), essential services (NIS2, the SOCI Act), government (PSPF, ISM, FISMA, the UAE IA Regulation) and defense supply chains (CMMC).

Explicit annual minimums appear in NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.14(a)(3), 5 CFR 930.301 for US federal systems, PSPF Requirement 0024, the DFSA and ADGM rulebooks for UAE free zone firms, and as a recommendation in Australia's ISM-0252.

Board level training is explicit in the EU: NIS2 Article 20(2) requires management body members to follow training, and DORA Article 5(4) requires regular specific training to keep ICT risk knowledge current.
This library does not yet document a Japanese cybersecurity training rule, so Japan is not compared here.
A multinational can standardize an annual, risk updated awareness program with phishing and social engineering content, then localize board training, role groups and record formats.

sections.heading: How do cybersecurity awareness training duties compare by market?

blocks.text: Every market covered here has explicit cyber training duties, but none has a single rule for all employers. The duty depends on whether the organization is a regulated financial entity, an operator of essential or critical services, a government body or a defense supplier. The table shows the main instruments as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Which organizations have an explicit cyber training duty?

blocks.text: Explicit duties fall on four groups: financial entities, essential and critical service operators, government bodies, and defense contractors. An ordinary commercial employer outside those groups usually has no cyber specific training rule, although privacy and security laws may imply one.

items: **Financial entities:** [APRA CPS 234](/regulations/apra-cps-234-security-awareness-training) in Australia, [DORA](/regulations/dora-ict-security-awareness-training) in the EU, [NYDFS Part 500](/regulations/nydfs-part-500-cybersecurity-training-requirements) in New York the [FTC Safeguards Rule](/regulations/ftc-safeguards-rule-employee-training) for US non bank institutions, and the [DFSA](/regulations/dfsa-training-and-competence-requirements) and [ADGM FSRA](/regulations/adgm-fsra-training-and-competence) rulebooks for UAE free zone firms.

**Essential and critical services:** [NIS2](/regulations/nis2-management-body-training) in the EU and, in Australia, the [SOCI Act CIRMP Rules](/regulations/soci-act-critical-infrastructure-personnel-training), which do not use the word training but require insider risk controls.

**Government:** Australia's [PSPF](/regulations/pspf-security-awareness-training) and [ISM](/regulations/ism-cyber-security-awareness-training), US [federal employee training under FISMA](/regulations/federal-employee-cybersecurity-awareness-training), and the [UAE IA Regulation](/regulations/uae-information-assurance-awareness-training) for government and critical entities.

**Defense supply chain:** [CMMC](/regulations/cmmc-security-awareness-training) Level 2 includes security awareness, role based training and insider threat awareness for contractors handling Controlled Unclassified Information; Level 1 has no training requirement.

sections.heading: Is annual cyber awareness training required?

blocks.text: Annual training is explicitly required in several instruments, but it is not universal: APRA, the FTC, NIS2 and the UAE IA controls leave the interval to the organization.

Section 500.14(a)(3) of the NYDFS regulation requires "periodic, but at a minimum annual" awareness training that includes social engineering, and the small entity exemption does not remove it. Under 5 CFR 930.301(a)(1), "All users of Federal information systems must be exposed to security awareness materials at least annually," and new employees before system access. PSPF Requirement 0024 requires training at engagement and annually for Commonwealth personnel including contractors, and ISM-0252 recommends annual training for all personnel. CMMC Level 3 adds training at hire, after a significant cyber event and at least annually.
In the UAE's financial free zones, DFSA rule GEN 5.5.14 and ADGM rule GEN 3.5.13 each require relevant employees to be trained at least annually under a comprehensive cyber training program.

sections.heading: Do boards and senior managers have to be trained?

blocks.text: Yes in the EU, where both NIS2 and DORA name management body training. Elsewhere, board knowledge is expected but framed as understanding rather than training.

NIS2 Article 20(2) requires members of management bodies to follow training so they can identify risks and assess cybersecurity risk management practices, and Portugal's Decree-Law 125/2025 requires management bodies to ensure regular training. DORA Article 5(4) requires management body members to keep their ICT risk knowledge current, "including by following specific training on a regular basis". In New York, 500.4(d)(1) requires the senior governing body to have sufficient understanding of cybersecurity to oversee the program, which may include the use of advisors. APRA's CPS 234 does not mandate a specific training course for boards or anyone else; its training expectations sit in the CPG 234 guide.

sections.heading: What should a multinational standardize and what should it localize?

blocks.text: Standardize an annual, risk updated awareness program for all staff with social engineering and phishing content, plus role based modules for privileged users and security staff. Localize board training, regulator specific topics and record formats.

blocks.text: Treating NIS2 and DORA board training as the global standard costs little and closes the largest structural gap between markets. For staff, the NYDFS rule is a good template everywhere: at least annual, includes social engineering, and updated from the risk assessment. A [role based training](/glossary/role-based-training) design keeps role overlays manageable, and [evidencing training effectiveness](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator) answers the effectiveness expectations in CPG 234, the UAE IA Regulation and EU Implementing Regulation 2024/2690.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each cyber instrument's training requirements as concepts, roles and assessment points before content is written, so one awareness core can carry sector and market overlays without duplicated courses. Each record links completion to the requirement it evidences. See [standards and accreditation](/platform/standards-accreditation).

faqs.q: Does every company need cybersecurity awareness training by law?
faqs.a: Not in the markets compared here. Explicit duties attach to financial entities, essential and critical service operators, government bodies and defense contractors. Other employers may still need training to meet general security or privacy duties, but no cyber specific rule names it for them.

faqs.q: Do small companies get an exemption from NYDFS training?
faqs.a: No. The limited exemption in 23 NYCRR 500.19(a) removes several monitoring requirements but not 500.14(a)(3), so small covered entities must still provide at least annual awareness training that includes social engineering.

faqs.q: How do NIS2 and DORA interact for EU banks?
faqs.a: NIS2 recognizes DORA as a sector specific act for financial entities, so EU banks and insurers follow DORA's ICT training rules: compulsory awareness and resilience modules for all employees and senior management, and regular specific training for management body members.

faqs.q: Is the UAE IA Regulation mandatory for private companies?
faqs.a: Only for entities designated critical under the UAE Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Policy, alongside government entities. Other UAE organizations may adopt it voluntarily. For those it binds, the awareness program and training needs analysis are Always Applicable controls.
